questions.q: What does the 'Anchor relative to' option do in a Relative Dates filter?
options: Pins 'today' to a fixed date instead of the actual calendar date the workbook is opened on
Converts the filter into a Range of Dates filter permanently
Deletes the filter after a set number of days
Has no real effect and is purely cosmetic
questions.explain: By default, a Relative Dates filter's 'today' is the real current date. Anchoring pins it to a fixed date, useful for consistent demos or screenshots.

questions.q: Why use a parameter to drive a Top N filter instead of hardcoding the number?
options: A viewer-facing parameter control lets someone change how many rows show (Top 5, Top 10, etc.) without editing the filter itself
Parameters make Top N filters run faster with no other benefit
Hardcoded Top N filters are not supported in Tableau at all
Parameters are required by Tableau for any filter to function
questions.explain: A parameter-driven Top N lets a dashboard viewer adjust N interactively — a hardcoded Top N filter requires editing the filter itself to change.

questions.q: Why does this lesson use a Set to build a parameter-driven Top N, rather than the plain dimension filter's Top tab?
options: Sets are more flexible — they can be combined with other sets and referenced in calculated fields, which a plain filter can't do
The Top tab on a dimension filter doesn't actually exist
Sets are simpler to build than a regular filter
Parameters can only be used with sets, never with filters
questions.explain: A Set gives you more downstream flexibility — combining with other sets and use inside calculated fields — that a plain dimension filter's Top tab doesn't offer.

questions.q: What does the Condition filter formula SUM([Sales]) > 10000, applied to Sub-Category, actually do?
options: Dynamically keeps only sub-categories whose total sales exceed $10,000, re-evaluating if the underlying data changes
Permanently deletes sub-categories under $10,000 from the data source
Filters individual order lines, not sub-categories
Has no effect unless combined with a Top N filter
questions.explain: A Condition filter evaluates the formula per value of the field it's applied to (Sub-Category here) and keeps only the ones where it's true — dynamically, unlike a fixed manual selection.

questions.q: What's the key difference between a Condition filter and a manual General-tab selection?
options: A Condition filter re-evaluates as the underlying data changes, so which values pass can change over time; a General-tab selection is a fixed, hardcoded list
Condition filters can only be used on measures, never dimensions
General-tab selections update automatically; Condition filters never do
There is no practical difference between the two
questions.explain: A Condition filter is formula-driven and dynamic; a General-tab selection is a fixed checklist that doesn't respond to changes in the underlying data.
